punchline: Maté cites a 95 percent remission rate among soldiers who were addicted in Vietnam and then came home.
thirty_sec: In 1971 the US government had a research group count what Vietnam's returning heroin addicts would cost. Most of those who had been dependent quit after coming home, and most without treatment. Gabor Maté reads that as proof that setting shapes addiction as much as the drug does. The 95 percent figure covers men who had been addicted, and the researchers themselves asked for more study.
